assessment.nobel_worthiness: Proton-coupled electron transfer is a physically stated mechanistic concept: concerted or stepwise proton and electron movement governs respiration, photosynthesis, water oxidation and electrocatalysis. The theory gives quantitative rate expressions and the experimental work gives clean model systems and bond-weakening thermochemistry. This is the kind of mechanism-in-physical-terms contribution I value most, and it is a field where I can judge the evidence directly.
assessment.attribution: Theory and experiment are separable. Hammes-Schiffer for the vibronic and multistate theory, Mayer for the experimental thermochemistry and conceptual framework of PCET, Nocera for PCET model systems and its application to artificial photosynthesis. Thomas J. Meyer is a legitimate early contributor, so the three-person limit forces a priority judgement that the expert reports would need to address.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of independent confirmation across enzymes, molecular catalysts and electrode interfaces. The concept is stable and widely used, so recognition is timely and not premature.
uncertainties: Priority between Meyer, Mayer and Nocera on the founding experimental concepts is not cleanly resolved.
The candidacy is a line of work, and the most decisive single discovery is less sharply defined than in a method prize.
I cannot independently verify every priority claim from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins showed, with engineered ruthenium-modified proteins and flash-quench kinetics, how distance and the protein medium set tunnelling rates, and later how hopping through aromatic residues protects enzymes. This underpins the understanding of electron flow in respiratory and photosynthetic complexes and is a clear case of physical mechanism applied to biology.
assessment.attribution: Gray is the dominant originator and the intellectual leader. Winkler is the long-term collaborator who carried the kinetics and the hopping work. A clean two-person configuration is possible, although the broader field (Marcus theory, Dutton's moving-electron rulers, Beratan and Onuchic tunnelling pathways) also contributed, and Marcus was already honoured in 1992.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and widely confirmed, with decades of consistent kinetics and structures. Risk is that recognition may be seen as late, or as overlapping with the earlier Marcus prize.
uncertainties: How much of the foundational credit belongs to others such as Dutton or Beratan is not resolved by the supplied credit list.
Whether the committee would see this as an extension of Marcus theory is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase catalyses the reduction of dinitrogen under ambient conditions through an extraordinary iron-molybdenum cofactor. Structures, including the central carbide and the turnover states, together with kinetic mechanism define one of the great remaining problems of bioinorganic chemistry. Importance to the nitrogen cycle is evident.
assessment.attribution: Rees led the crystallographic structure and the cofactor structure work, Einsle resolved the interstitial carbide at high resolution, and Seefeldt with Dean developed the kinetic and mechanistic framework. Dean, Ribbe and others have claims as well, so a three-person limit leaves real allocation problems.
assessment.maturity: Structure is mature and replicated. The reaction mechanism, including how N2 binds and what the E4 state does, is still being worked out, so the field is only partly settled.
uncertainties: The catalytic mechanism is not fully settled, which could make a prize premature.
Allocation among Rees, Dean, Seefeldt, Ribbe and Einsle is contested.
Whether a structure and mechanism prize should be anchored in the cofactor or in the reaction kinetics is open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory with the principle of minimal frustration gave a physical picture of how proteins fold, and Fersht's protein engineering and phi-value analysis made transition states experimentally accessible. The concept fits my preference for physical principles that are tested by kinetics. It has influenced structure prediction and folding thinking generally.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the main theorists of the funnel landscape, and Fersht is the clear experimental pioneer. Bryngelson and Dill have strong claims on earlier foundations, so the allocation is not clean.
assessment.maturity: Concept is well-established and has been validated by experiment and simulation. The 2024 prize for protein structure prediction and design lowers urgency but also leaves folding theory as a natural complement.
uncertainties: Credit split between Wolynes, Onuchic, Bryngelson and Dill is disputed.
Whether the committee will treat folding as already served by the 2024 prize is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders introduce a new chemical modality: induced proximity to hijack the ubiquitin-proteasome system and remove proteins. The chemistry is of real consequence, the mechanism is increasingly understood structurally, and compounds are in advanced clinical development.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies established the PROTAC concept, and Handa identified cereblon as the thalidomide target that made the molecular glue and clinical story coherent. Ciulli, Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim all have important claims, which makes the three-person allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Concept confirmed by many groups, but clinical proof of the modality is still maturing, so recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Late-stage clinical outcomes are not yet settled.
Allocation among Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Gray and others is uncertain.
The thalidomide and cereblon discovery may be better treated as a separate compound element.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables diffraction before damage and time-resolved structural movies of reacting proteins at room temperature. This directly matches the combination of time-resolved methods and structure that makes mechanisms visible, including photosystem II and light-driven proteins.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof of principle and the methods, Fromme the membrane-protein and photosystem applications with Spence, Schlichting the time-resolved biochemical applications. Hajdu contributed the conceptual foundation. The credit set is strong but spread across the originating collaboration.
assessment.maturity: The method is validated and in wide use, though the largest scientific payoffs, such as routine mechanistic movies, are still arriving, and it depends on large facilities.
uncertainties: Founding collaboration is large and credit for the original concept is distributed.
Method impact relative to cryo-EM and synchrotron serial methods is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional heteronuclear NMR and isotope-labelling strategies made it possible to determine the structures and dynamics of large biomolecules in solution, giving direct access to motion on timescales relevant to function. The methods are central to modern biophysical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Bax, Kay and Clore are the leading figures for development and application of triple-resonance and TROSY-related methods, and dynamics. Wagner and Palmer have significant claims, and Wüthrich already received the 2002 prize for NMR structures, which complicates novelty.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and widely validated, but the earlier Nobel recognition of NMR biomolecular structure may reduce the case for a new award.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2002 prize for NMR structure determination of biomolecules.
Priority and allocation among Bax, Clore, Kay, Wagner and Palmer is not clean.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organizing principle of cells has opened a new view of intracellular compartmentation with a physical-chemical description. The field is fast-moving and conceptually influential.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed phase separation of P granules and nucleoli, and Rosen showed multivalent interactions driving phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed physical and sequence-based principles. This is a plausible three-person set, though the field is broad.
assessment.maturity: Younger and still contested in terms of the physiological relevance of condensates and how they are defined. Recognition may be premature, and the biological side may fit another prize.
uncertainties: Debate on whether many reported condensates are physiologically meaningful.
Whether this is chemistry or physiology is a committee judgement.
Credit is distributed across physics, biology and chemistry contributors.
